question: Why Are Related and Upsell Products So Expensive to Query?
metaDescription: Finding related products by shared categories/tags requires a genuinely complex query, which gets progressively slower as the catalog grows larger.
shortAnswer: Automatically calculated related products (based on shared categories and tags, when no manual upsell/cross-sell is explicitly set) require a genuinely complex database query comparing the current product against the entire rest of the catalog to find suitable matches, and this query's cost scales with catalog size — a store with a few hundred products barely notices it, but one with tens of thousands can see this become a genuinely measurable slowdown on every single product page.

image.alt: Automatically calculated related products requiring an expensive query that scales with catalog size

bodyHtml:
Why This Query Is Expensive

Finding related products isn't a simple lookup — it requires comparing the current product's categories and tags against every other product in the catalog to identify overlaps, then ranking and selecting a suitable subset to display. Unlike a straightforward query filtering by a single indexed value, this comparison-based matching is inherently more computationally expensive, and that cost grows as the total number of products to compare against grows.

Ways to Reduce This Cost

  • Manually setting upsells and cross-sells on key, high-traffic products bypasses the automatic calculation entirely for those specific products, since a manually curated list requires no expensive comparison query.
  • Object caching can cache the related products result for a given product, so the expensive calculation only runs once rather than on every single page view.
  • Reducing the number of related products shown slightly reduces query and rendering cost, though the underlying comparison cost is the bigger factor.
  • A dedicated recommendation engine or plugin designed for large catalogs can offer a more efficient (and often more relevant) alternative to core WooCommerce's built-in related-products logic at scale.

Addressing This

  1. Manually curate upsells/cross-sells for your highest-traffic products where practical.
  2. Enable object caching so the related-products calculation isn't repeated unnecessarily.
  3. Consider a dedicated recommendation solution if the catalog is large enough that this remains a genuine bottleneck.
